full_judgment:
This Rule at the instance of the plaintiff- appellant-petitioner calls in question judgment and decree dated 27-10-93 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka, in Title Appeal No. 80 of 1972 affirming the judgment and decree dated 29-1-92 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, 3rd Court of Additional Assistant Judge, Dhaka, in Title Suit No. 21 of 1989 dismissing the suit. 

 5. Since the defendants-respondents-opposite parties Nos. 1 & 2 evicted the family members of the plaintiff-appellant-petitioner on 6-1-88 by police force after receipt of the show cause notice, the plaintiff-appellant-petitioner vide order dated 1-8-89 amended the plaint praying for a decree of mandatory injunction for restoration of possession of the suit property to the plaintiff-appellant-petitioner by removing defendant No. 3 who was also added as defendant No. 3 by the said amendment. 

 7. Plaintiff-appellant-petitioner examined two PWs including himself as PW 1 and 1 DW was examined on behalf of the Government in support of their respective case. Both the trial Court as well as the appellate Court below dismissed the suit on the finding that the plaintiff-appellant-petitioner and his wife were not residing in the suit property, rather the suit property was under illegal occupation of some unauthorised persons and, as such, the plaintiff-appellant-petitioner was not entitled to the decree for restoration of possession by removing defendant No. 3 from the suit property. 

 9. Mrs. Suraiya Begum, learned Assistant Attorney-General appearing for the Government, submits that since the plaintiff-appellant-petitioner was found absent from the suit property on the date of aforesaid enquiries the government was entitled to evict unauthorised occupants without any prior notice of eviction and it was accordingly, done. Learned Assistant Attorney-General further contends that since the possession of the suit property was already handed over to the defendant No.3 during the pendency of the suit, plaintiffs prayer for decree by way of mandatory injunction for restoration of possession of the suit property to the plaintiff-appellant-petitioner by amendment cannot be sustained in law and, as such, the courts below rightly refused to decree the suit. 

 12. When a party to a suit by an act brings about a change in the existing state of affairs, a party aggrieved by such change is competent in law to mould his prayer/relief to suit his need in keeping with the changed situation in the interest of maintenance of the suit. The Court may, in an appropriate case, in exercise of its inherent power, require the offending party to restore the status quo ante by issuing a temporary injunction in mandatory form. If at all any authority is needed in this connection the case of Abdul Jalil and another vs. Abu Bakar Siddique reported in 35 DLR (AD) 42 may be referred to. In this view of the matter it is held that the plaintiff-appellant-petitioner was competent to amend his plaint praying for a decree for mandatory injunction in the facts and circumstances of the present case because such amendment is necessary for determination of the real controversy in the suit. 

 16. Even where there is no law concerning recovery of possession of any government building the principle of natural justice ought to have been complied with. Because principle of natural justice is also applicable in administrative matters as natural justice demands that before a person is proceeded against he should know the allegations against him and, as such, he should be given an opportunity of explaining his position in the matter. Since the government has failed to issue any notice before eviction in question, plaintiff-appellant-petitioner is entitled to a decree in the suit. 

 17. In the result, the Rule is made absolute and the Title Suit No. 21 of 1989 is hereby decreed. Opposite party government namely, Ministry of Works is directed to restore the plaintiff-appellant-petitioner to the possession of the suit property within two months from the receipt of this order. Send an advance copy of this order to the Ministry of Works.
